page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-standard-64 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance built on the 64-bit Arm (arm64) architecture. The configuration supplies 64 dedicated vCPUs alongside 256 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 processor-to-memory ratio of 4 GB per virtual core. It operates without hardware-based accelerators, offering zero GPUs.

Storage on the c4a-standard-64 relies entirely on external network-attached volumes, as the instance includes no local storage disks. Network setups must also account for zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses bundled with the instance by default. The dedicated core allocation ensures consistent compute performance without virtualization-level thread contention from neighboring tenants.

By leveraging an Arm-based CPU foundation, this instance delivers high core density and balanced memory allocation suited for horizontally scalable infrastructure. It offers qualitative operational efficiency for large-scale production workloads that support AArch64 execution, such as distributed application microservices, database clusters, container nodes, and continuous integration runners.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4a-standard-64 is an Arm-based general-purpose instance delivering 64 dedicated vCPUs and 256 GB of system RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 resource ratio of 4 GB per core. Operating on the arm64 architecture, it does not include discrete GPUs and possesses no integrated local storage, requiring network-attached storage solutions for all persistent filesystems and operating system images. Zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default. The dedicated allocation of 64 virtual cores provides steady compute capability without multitenant CPU sharing. The c4a-standard-64 is structured for enterprise container clusters, large-scale multi-threaded web application hosting, caching tiers, continuous integration pipelines, and data processing environments compiled for AArch64 systems.
